newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks end mixed as blue chips reverse.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks end mixed as blue chips reverse.

text.p: Reversing several strong sessions, Kuala Lumpur blue chips ended weaker as profit-takers came in to reap gains. But small-capitalisation shares finished higher amid speculative play, dealers said.

Turnover remained hectic amid a fresh influx of funds following two long festival breaks. "We were on the buyside," said Ralph Dixon, of TA Securities' international division. "There were not many features, but people were focused on the second liners."
The Composite Index ended off 3.36 points to 1,262.86, above its 1,259.40 session low.
But the Second Board index added 4.34 points to 650.69.
Total volume was 697 million shares, versus 732 million on Thursday. Gainers topped losers by 391 to 233.

Low-valued stocks remained top attractions as investors searched for potential winners. "The trend is apparently for smaller-cap stocks like Suria Capital, Ann Joo and Sinora," said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities.
But among the blue chips, "it's profit-taking," she said. "The market has been going up quite strongly."
